Assess engineers on coding tasks on the same platform
Engineers take the Tech section, the second section of Skills Intelligence. Your people team sees engineering results in the same place as the results of business teams.

Passed test cases and task difficulty set a proficiency level for each assessed skill. Skills Intelligence uses a five-level scale from novice to expert.
Your engineering leaders can review a proficiency level per skill next to the results of your business teams.

Frequently asked questions about AI skills assessment and reskilling
An AI skills assessment platform tests whether people can complete a work task with AI and scores the result. Codility Skills Intelligence runs AI skills assessments for the knowledge workers you already employ, in business functions and in engineering.
Look for three things: realistic tasks, a scoring method the vendor can explain, and coverage of the roles you need. Codility Skills Intelligence gives employees realistic tasks to complete with AI and scores each output deterministically. Confirm task coverage for your job families when you plan the pilot.
Codility Skills Intelligence gives your people team a scored output from each employee who completes a task with AI. Your team can report the results to the board by function, by team and by employee.
An AI skills test on a real task records the output an employee produced with AI. A self-report questionnaire records how the employee rates their own confidence. Your people team can review the output and its score.
An AI skill assessment in Skills Intelligence can cover business roles and engineering roles. AI for Business covers business functions, and general workforce tasks cover roles without role-specific tasks. The Tech section covers software engineering areas including web, backend, mobile, data, cloud and DevOps.
No. An AI skills assessment platform measures skills, and a learning platform delivers training. Your people team uses the Skills Intelligence results to decide who takes which course in the learning platform you already run.
Assess before you assign. Employees complete a realistic task with AI before the reskilling program starts. Your people team then reviews the AI skills gap in each team. Your team assigns reskilling to the employees whose results show a gap.
No. Codility scores each output deterministically, and no generative model assigns the score. The evidence behind the scoring is published in

Yes. Each employee sees assessed results in a personal profile.
Introduce the assessment as a development step. Explain to employees how your team will use the results. Codility provides a change-management and communications template for the rollout.
